title: Bristol Stool Chart Guide
subtitle: Understand stool consistency and its meaning for your UC
selectPrompt: Tap any card to select it directly into your daily log

headerTip.title: How to interpret this in your daily routine?
headerTip.desc: Type 4 represents the stool consistency considered smooth and balanced. Types 6 & 7 indicate faster transit time, where staying well hydrated and logging notes is helpful.

type1.title: Type 1: Separate hard lumps
type1.shapeDesc: Hard, dry little balls resembling nuts, difficult to pass and requiring straining.
type1.clinicalMeaning: Constipation. The colon has absorbed most water. May require straining.
type1.actionTip: Increase your daily fluid intake and speak with your doctor regarding suitable soluble fibers.

type2.title: Type 2: Lumpy sausage-shaped
type2.shapeDesc: Firm cylindrical mass with multiple compacted lumps and an irregular surface.
type2.clinicalMeaning: Mild constipation. Compacted stool indicating slower transit.
type2.actionTip: Maintain steady hydration throughout the day and avoid holding bowel movement urges.

type3.title: Type 3: Sausage-shaped with cracks
type3.shapeDesc: Long sausage shape with shallow surface fissures, passing easily without strain.
type3.clinicalMeaning: Healthy, balanced consistency. Indicates proper hydration.
type3.actionTip: Excellent consistency. Continue with your regular diet and wellness routine.

type4.title: Type 4: Smooth, soft snake or sausage
type4.shapeDesc: Soft, smooth sausage shape. Slides out effortlessly with zero pain or straining.
type4.clinicalMeaning: Ideal! Represents smooth, soft, and balanced stool consistency.
type4.actionTip: Great pattern! Maintain your healthy habits and regular follow-up with your doctor.

type5.title: Type 5: Soft blobs with clear-cut edges
type5.shapeDesc: Soft pasty pieces with distinct, well-defined borders that pass easily.
type5.clinicalMeaning: Tendency toward loose stools. Bowel transit is somewhat faster.
type5.actionTip: Monitor subsequent bowel trips and increase daily water and fluid intake.

type6.title: Type 6: Fluffy, mushy pieces with ragged edges
type6.shapeDesc: Pasty, shapeless stool with torn, ragged fragments and lacking solid form.
type6.clinicalMeaning: Loose stools. Common during digestive sensitivity or dietary changes.
type6.actionTip: Avoid processed or irritating foods, hydrate with water and electrolyte drinks, and track blood/mucus.

type7.title: Type 7: Watery, entirely liquid with no solids
type7.shapeDesc: Completely watery and fluid consistency, with no solid chunks whatsoever.
type7.clinicalMeaning: Entirely liquid stool. The bowel is not retaining fluids adequately.
type7.actionTip: Pay attention to hydration! Drink water and electrolyte solutions. If persistent, consult your physician.
